title: Knock a part out of a sorting nest down the drop-through that has the tote under it
instruction: Knock the part out of the nest into the yellow tote.
context: Done by: machine feeders and offbearers, and inspectors and sorters (O*NET 53-7063, 51-9061). On a sorting nest the batch's tote is set under one drop-through; a part sent down another lands in scrap and cannot be pulled back up. Unlike TK-XPZZLV (load the machine its stack light marks ready) and TK-7JGQ27 (set gates for a named bin), the cue is where the part will land: the robot must push the knock-out on the far side of the tote, and a wrong push cannot be undone.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Sorting nest (fixed, light-grey steel): a block 156 mm front to back (22.2 to 37.8 cm in front of the arm bases) and 216 mm wide (10.8 cm each side of the midline), 92 mm tall. Inside it, a cross-shaped channel 40 mm wide with its floor 50 mm up, under a 6 mm roof from 86 to 92 mm up (36 mm headroom). One arm of the cross runs left to right, 25 to 29 cm in front of the arm bases, from 9.6 cm left to 9.6 cm right of the midline; the other runs front to back along the midline from 23.4 to 36.6 cm in front of the arm bases. They meet at the centre, 27 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline. Three drop-throughs, open from above through the roof, cut the channel floor: left (3.0 to 8.0 cm left of the midline, 25 to 29 cm out), right (the mirror image) and far (30 to 35 cm out, 2 cm each side of the midline). Under each is a bore of the same size down to a 4 mm black plate on the table. A dark 6 mm stripe on the roof marks each knob's path. Part (loose): an aluminium cylinder 20 mm across and 28 mm tall, 60 g, standing upright on the channel floor at the centre. Knock-outs (steel, 50 g moving, no spring, damped at 2 N per m/s, with end stops): each a blade 36 mm wide, 8 mm thick and 30 mm tall riding 2 mm above the channel floor, with a 6 mm stem up through the roof to a red knob 20 x 20 mm, 98 to 122 mm up. The left one's knob is 8.8 cm left of the midline, 27 cm out; it slides 130 mm toward the right and pushes the part down the right drop-through. The right one is its mirror image. The near one's knob is on the midline 24.2 cm out; it slides 70 mm forward and pushes the part down the far drop-through. Tote (loose, yellow plastic, 0.4 kg): 38 mm square and 43 mm tall, 2 mm walls on a 4 mm floor, standing on a bore's black plate with its rim 3 mm below the channel floor and its side 1 mm from the bore wall nearest the centre. Lot A (the screenshot): the tote is in the right bore, centred 27 cm out and 5.0 cm right of the midline. Lot B: in the left bore, 5.0 cm left of the midline. Lot C: in the far bore, centred 32 cm out on the midline. Each drop-through is 42 mm deep from the roof top to the channel floor, so in the top camera only a strip of the tote's yellow shows at the far side of its drop-through; it shows fully from straight above. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Pass/fail, judged over the whole trial from the video and a photo. Score 1.0 when, at the end, the part is in the tote: its centre inside the tote's 34 mm square inner walls, above the tote's floor and below its rim, and its top below the channel floor; the part and the tote are still (under 1 cm/s), no part of either gripper is within 5 mm of the part, and this has held for 3 s. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any point the part's bottom goes more than 5 mm below the channel floor anywhere but over the tote (down a bare drop-through), or the tote moves more than 5 mm or tilts more than 10 degrees from where it stood. Moving a knob is never a fault in itself: pulling back a knob started the wrong way, before the part drops, is allowed. Score 0 in every other case: the part still in the channel, on the nest, caught on the tote's rim with its top above the channel floor, or still held. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Lift the part out of the tote (or the bore) and stand it upright at the channel centre. Slide the three knock-outs back to their outer stops. For lot A stand the tote in the right bore, for lot B in the left bore and for lot C in the far bore, against the bore wall nearest the centre. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Everything is rigid boxes and a cylinder. The nest is a bench-scale mock-up of a sorting nest: the knock-outs are plain slides with end stops, light damping and no spring, and the bores stand in for the chutes to scrap. The tote is moved between lots with the layout, not by a person mid-trial. Masses and friction are the simulator's values. The three lots stop a fixed habit (always one knob), not a memorised replay of all three layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C; the right arm hovered over the nest and the tote's drop-through but pushed no knob, and the part stayed in the channel); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A, B and C. Both videos show the first trial, lot A.
